To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) The eukaryotic orthologs of the prokaryotic translation initiation factors IF1 and 2, eIF1A, and eIF5, interact physically and functionally.
the eukaryotic orthologs of the prokaryotic translation initiation factors IF1 and I F2 interact directly in vivo and in vitro.
eIF1A interacts with eIF5B, and the eif5B C-terminal region is required for eIF1A-eIF5B interaction and for eIF5B function.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanism of translation in eukaryotic cells and the role of initiation factors in the process.
the mechanism of protein synthesis and its regulation in eukaryotic cells.
the mechanisms of protein synthesis and the factors that control this process.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the interaction between IF2 and IF1 is important for translation initiation and that this interaction is conserved between prokaryotes, where it has been studied in detail, and eukaryotes.
the physical and functional interaction between the eukaryotic orthologs of Pro-karyotic Translation Initiaton Factors IF1 and 2 is essential for translation initiation.
eIF1A interacts physically with eIF5B, and this interaction is critical for the growth of the cell.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
eIF1A is required for the function of eIF5 in yeast.
the interaction between eIF1A/IF1 and eIF5/IF2 is critical for the initiation step in eukaryotic translation.
eIF1A is a novel eukaryotic factor that binds to the C-terminal domain of eIF5 and that the eIF1AEIF5B interaction is important for the function of the eIF5 complex.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the physical interaction of eIF1 and eIF5 in prokaryotic cells and the physical interaction of the eukaryotic orthologs, eIF1A, eIF5, and eIF5b is conserved and plays an important role for translation initiation.
the eIF1/eIF1A and the eIF5/eIF5B proteins have a conserved physical and functional relationship.

we have found a physical interaction between eIF1A, a protein that is required for translation initiation, and eIF5b, a protein that catalyzes the release of the 60S ribosomal subunit from the 80S ribosome during the initiation of translation in eukaryotic cells.
